title: Filip Jorgensen asks to leave Chelsea, club open to offers for goalkeeper
content:
Goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen wants to leave Chelsea and the club are open to offers for him this summer.

Having spent the majority of the 2025-26 season as understudy to Robert Sanchez, sources with knowledge of the situation, speaking on the condition of anonymity, told The Athletic that the Denmark international has made Chelsea aware that he is keen to find regular game time elsewhere this summer.

Sources also confirmed that Chelsea are prepared to sell the 24-year-old, who joined from Villarreal for €24.5million (£20.7m, $26.6m) in the summer of 2024, on favourable terms and do not need to sign a replacement, with Belgian prospect Mike Penders set to join the first-team squad this summer after a season-long loan at BlueCo sister club Strasbourg.

Penders, 20, is one of the most highly-rated young goalkeepers in Europe and is expected to be given a chance to compete with Sanchez for the No 1 spot under incoming manager Xabi Alonso.

Jorgensen was also recruited to provide competition for Sanchez. He has made 34 appearances across all competitions in his two seasons at Chelsea, but more of those have come in the UEFA Conference League (12) than the Premier League (11).

Former head coach Liam Rosenior handed Jorgensen a surprise start for Chelsea ahead of Sanchez against Paris Saint-Germain in the first leg of the Champions League round of 16, but the Dane’s loose pass to Bradley Barcola resulted in a goal at Parc des Princes.

Analysis by Chelsea correspondent Liam Twomey

Chelsea supporters may be anxious about the club’s biggest players looking to leave Stamford Bridge this summer, but it’s fair to say Jorgensen doesn’t move that particular needle.

He arrived to little fanfare from Villarreal two years ago and has not proven himself an upgrade on predecessor Djordje Petrovic, never mind first-choice goalkeeper Sanchez.

High-profile errors — most notably presenting the ball to Barcola in Parc des Princes — have eroded any faith that he is the answer to what remains something of a problem position for Chelsea. Jorgensen can justifiably contend that no goalkeeper can perform at their best when denied the rhythm and familiarity with team-mates that comes from regular football.

A move this summer would suit all parties. Chelsea need to raise funds for their own transfer plans and to make room in the first-team squad for Penders, whose development at Strasbourg and senior international recognition for Belgium is a source of pride and excitement at Stamford Bridge. He looks to have a very bright future.

Jorgensen should command interest from clubs in England and in Europe prepared to offer him a No 1 job, and Chelsea’s asking price should not be a barrier to a sale.
